text:
Maya L.: kicked off a short benchmark across two node types to compare interconnect effects (SXM with NVLink vs hostbus/PCIe). model: redwood-13b-qlora, quantized 4-bit (GPTQ-like). summary below, attaching quick numbers and repro.
Kevin P.: link to dashboard https://grafana.internal/r/bench/1745 (summary chart). :eyes:
Aditya R.: raw numbers I extracted:
- SXM (same node, NVLink): p50 latency = 18ms, p95 = 33ms, throughput = ~13k tok/s (batch=8)
- Hostbus (PCIe, same server but no NVLink): p50 = 28ms, p95 = 60ms, throughput = ~9k tok/s
- Cross-socket (no NVLink, different socket, default OS scheduling): p50 = 52ms, p95 = 110ms, throughput = ~5.5k tok/s
Quality: quantized model had ~0.6% BLEU drop vs fp16 on our eval set; consistent across interconnects.
Sanjay K.: ran `nvidia-smi topo -m` and saw NVLink links present on SXM nodes, absent on hostbus ones. Also pinned worker threads with numactl which helped on hostbus. snippet I used:
```
numactl --physcpubind=0-15 --membind=0 \ 
  python run_infer.py --model redwood-13b-q4 --batch 8 --kernel flash-attn-v2
```
When I removed numa pinning p50 on hostbus jumped ~8-12%.
bench-bot: job 68234 finished: sxm-run-1 (completed), hostbus-run-1 (completed). artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/68234/{sxm,hostbus}/
Maya L.: repro steps I pushed to the repo: set `REDWOOD_KERNEL_SEL=auto` to let runtime pick flash-attn where available. if you want manual:
```
export REDWOOD_KERNEL_SEL=flash-attn-v2
python -m redwood.bench.runner --model redwood-13b-q4 --profile --batch 8 --duration 120
```
Also note: for PCIe hosts add `numactl --localalloc` to keep memory on the same NUMA node as the GPU.
Kevin P.: curious about kernel fallback: when flash-attn is disabled on SXM throughput drops ~20% but latency p95 barely changes. on hostbus fallback often means memcpys across sockets which explodes p95.
Aditya R.: short takeaways:
- NVLink (SXM) removes most inter-GPU memcpy overhead; runtime should prefer shared-memory kernels there.
- NUMA pinning matters for PCIe hosts; default scheduler can place CPU <-> GPU memory on different nodes.
- Quantization cost is orthogonal to interconnect, but performance delta between SXM/PCIe grows with batch size since batching exposes memcpy hotspots.
Sanjay K.: opening an internal issue to add detection: if `nvidia-smi topo -m` shows NVLink, set kernel preference to shared-memory. add a host check that warns when GPUs are on different NUMA nodes.
Maya L.: thanks — I'll update the onboarding doc for new model bring-ups to include these checks and a short checklist (nvlink present?, numa pin?, kernel sel). :white_check_mark:
Kevin P.: sounds good. next step: run region-to-region tests to see if inter-region latency dominates for small models or if intra-node topology still matters for larger models. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
